patch.value: Surface pending field-aware merge-decision receipts in pm brief

When the field-aware merge driver discards a peer agent's scalar edit during a merge, the decision is recorded as a pending receipt in .git/pm-merge-receipts, but pm validate reports ok:true and never mentions it (unbraind/pm-cli#770) — so an agent resuming after a merge loads a context that silently omits the peer's work. This feature surfaces pending receipts in brief / brief prompt / brief diverge: compromised items get an inline ⚠ merge marker in focus/next, a dedicated ## ⚠ Pending Merge Decisions section lists the discarded field/value, and brief diverge adds pm merge reconcile to recommended next steps. Receipts are read via @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/merge; each receipt item_path has its stray wrapping single-quote layer stripped (unbraind/pm-cli#771 — Git wraps the %P path). The common case (no pending receipts) stays silent.

New MergeDecisionsSummary, MergeDecisionEntry, BriefItem.mergeCompromised types and collectPendingMergeDecisions/mergeDecisionsIsEmpty exports are added over @unbrained/pm-cli/sdk/merge with zero 'any' in index.ts; A real conflicting two-branch git merge fixture drives pending receipts through the registered brief and brief diverge commands in markdown and json (no mocks); item_path wrapping-quote normalization for upstream pm-cli#771 is covered end-to-end against a real receipt; A long discarded value is truncated to 120 chars + ellipsis so it cannot blow the token budget; lossless union collections are not reported as conflicts; Clean-workspace quiet path: no merge section, no ⚠ merge marker, no mergeDecisions block, and no pm merge reconcile recommendation; npm run build && npm run typecheck && npm run check && npm test pass (150/150) and npm run changelog:check reports up to date

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Verified by claude-code with a production proof rather than trusting the unit tests: built extension installed into a throwaway workspace with a REAL two-branch conflicting merge. The collection path correctly maps the real receipt — brief --json reports mergeDecisions.pendingCount 1 with itemId, the normalized itemPath .agents/pm/tasks/<id>.toon carrying no quotes per upstream 771, preferred ours, and conflicts[].discarded holding the peer value. brief diverge --json carries the same section, the cross-reference marker renders as a leading warn merge <id> on the affected item, and a clean workspace adds zero merge-decision output.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: Found and fixed a PRE-EXISTING defect while proving this feature: pm brief --json returned MARKDOWN. The handler read --json from ctx.options, but --json is a host-owned global the CLI consumes into ctx.global, so the check never matched and pm brief --json piped to jq failed on a parse error at the # pm brief heading. Confirmed pre-existing by rebuilding origin/main and reproducing. Fixed by a resolveBriefFormat helper applied at all six format-resolution sites; an explicit --format still wins in both directions. Not a regression from this branch but fixed here because it is the same output path and it is what makes the new merge-decision data reachable through pm's universal convention.

value.author: claude-code
value.text: One pre-existing test had to state its intent explicitly: the SDK test harness defaults globals to json true quiet true noPager true, so a test asserting MARKDOWN was previously passing only because the handler ignored the global. It now passes global json false. Added a contract test pinning the fix, falsification-checked: reverting the helper to the options-only read fails it (150 pass 1 fail) and restoring passes (151 pass 0 fail).

patch.value: pm brief and pm brief diverge surface pending merge-decision receipts collected from real receipts with item id, conflicting fields and the truncated discarded value; the affected item carries a cross-reference marker; a clean workspace adds no output; the upstream 771 quoted item_path is normalized and never leaks; pm brief --json emits parseable JSON via the host-owned global while an explicit --format wins; 151 tests pass with zero any.
Shipped: pending merge decisions are now visible at brief time, plus a pre-existing --json global defect fixed in the same output path.
